newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Telecom firms tight-lipped over Vietnam deal.
newsitem.headline: Telecom firms tight-lipped over Vietnam deal.

text.p: Vietnam Post and Telecommunications Corporation (VNPT) has signed deals with three foreign firms for a major upgrading of the telecoms infrastructure in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, an official Vietnam daily reported on Tuesday.
The Saigon Times Daily reported that Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc, France Telecom, Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone have struck deals with VNPT worth together more than $900 million.
The newspaper said a Business Cooperation Contract would also be signed with Australia's Telstra in the near future.
But executives at all four firms declined to comment on Tuesday, while VNPT officials refused to answer phone calls.
Negotiations between VNPT and foreign companies for the upgrading of Vietnam's primitive telecommunications system have been underway for several years.

The first to reach agreement was South Korea's state-owned Korea Telecom, which announced in May it had signed a $40 million deal to install a telephone network in the northern port town of Haiphong and two neighbouring provinces.
The latest reported deals are much bigger and involve the upgrading of telecoms facilities in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.
Saigon Times Daily said NTT and Cable and Wireless will develop some 500,000 lines in Hanoi, while Telstra and France Telecom will build the Ho Chi Minh City network of up to a million lines.

VNPT officials have said Vietnam needs around $3.5 billion to develop its telecoms infrastructure with a view to increasing the number of phone lines nationwide from 1.5 per 100 people to five or six per 100 by the year 2000.

The deals with the foreign firms form part of that sum and will allow them to share revenue with VNPT, which has said it is hoping to raise funds for further development through overseas resources including a possible future international bond issue.
